# OS Update Channel and Customer Fleet — v0

## Vision

Genome's Agentic OS will be installed in many places: operator workstations, customer laptops, customer servers, and disposable VMs spun up by build-runners. Each install is a hand-edited tree on disk. We need a way to: (a) know what versions are running where, (b) ship safe updates without breaking customer-local work, (c) refuse to leak customer data while doing so, and (d) recover when an update goes wrong.

The update model is **manifest-pull, not push**. Installs read a signed manifest from a canonical source on a schedule they control. The control plane never opens a connection into a customer install. Telemetry is opt-in by channel, fixed-schema, redacted by construction (the redaction is a schema validator, not a regex pass), and bounded in size. Risky changes (executables, hooks, MCP configs, permission grants) never auto-apply on customer roots — they require an explicit signed approval token from the operator OR a policy declaration in `UPDATE_POLICY.md` that names the migration id.

The v1 milestone is: an operator can see a dashboard of installed fleet state, ship a safe-additive update to all stable-channel customers without operator action per-install, and roll any install back to the prior version in one CLI command using state stored on disk on that install.

## Architecture

### Layout (installed root)

```
~/agentic_os/
  .agentic_root                       sentinel; absence ⇒ refuse all update ops
  agentic-os.package.json             pinned package + channel + install_id
  agentic-os.lock.json                installed packages, versions, checksums, source manifest URL+sha
  agentic-os.local.json               operator/customer overrides; NEVER overwritten by updates
  UPDATE_POLICY.md                    human-readable + machine-parseable frontmatter
  registries/
    updates.yml                       channel, policy, last_check, last_apply, heartbeat_url
    capabilities.yml                  declared capabilities (drives capability_hash)
  06-runs-and-logs/updates/<ts>/      one dir per apply attempt; never deleted by update code
```

### Component boundaries (factories, ports)

```
types/update.types.ts            UpdateManifest, UpdatePlan, ApplyResult, PolicyDecision (discriminated unions)
adapters/manifest.http.adapter.ts  fetch + verify signed manifest from HTTPS
adapters/manifest.git.adapter.ts   fetch from git tag of source repo
adapters/telemetry.https.adapter.ts POST redacted heartbeat
adapters/telemetry.noop.adapter.ts  default for `pinned` channel
ports/manifest.port.ts            ManifestPort.fetch(channel) → UpdateManifest
ports/telemetry.port.ts           TelemetryPort.send(HeartbeatPayload) — payload schema enforced at port boundary
data/update/
  update.types.ts                 PlanItem (additive_file | overwrite_file | exec_change | mcp_change | hook_change | permission_change | migration)
  policy.evaluator.ts             pure: (PlanItem[], Policy, UPDATE_POLICY.md.frontmatter) → PolicyDecision per item
  plan.builder.ts                 pure: (lock, manifest, fs-state) → UpdatePlan
  redactor.ts                     pure: (RawHeartbeat) → HeartbeatPayload | RedactionError; schema-validated, not regex
  rollback.snapshot.ts            copy-before-write; SHA-pinned manifest of changed paths
  apply.executor.ts               applies one PlanItem at a time inside a write-lock
  heartbeat.service.ts            builds + sends Heartbeat; no FS writes outside updates/<ts>/
jobs/update.heartbeat.job.ts      scheduled; per-channel cadence; rate-limited
init/                             composition root: wires adapters by channel
```

**Layer rule:** `data/update/` never imports `adapters/` directly; manifest and telemetry come through ports. Tests pass fake ports; no network in unit tests.

### Deterministic policy evaluator

The policy evaluator is the trust gate. It is a pure function with no I/O. Given a list of PlanItems, the active `Policy`, and the parsed `UPDATE_POLICY.md` frontmatter, it returns one `PolicyDecision` per item. `PolicyDecision` is one of: `AUTO_APPLY`, `REQUIRES_APPROVAL { reason, approval_kind: signed_token | policy_declaration }`, `BLOCKED { reason }`. The apply executor refuses to run any item whose decision is not `AUTO_APPLY` OR whose `REQUIRES_APPROVAL` has not been satisfied by an approval artifact present on disk (signed token at `registries/approvals/<migration_id>.token`, or a `permits:` entry in `UPDATE_POLICY.md` frontmatter naming the exact migration id).

This is what makes "auto-apply is safe" not a forecast: every PlanItem must literally pass through `policy.evaluator.ts` and the executor's match-or-refuse check. There is no path that applies an item without a decision.

### Redactor as schema, not filter

`HeartbeatPayload` is a Zod schema with a closed set of fields (install_id, os_name, installed_version, channel, capability_hash, last_update_check, doctor_summary{ok,blockers,warnings}, optional customer_id). The redactor builds a payload by **constructing from named fields**, never by copying or stripping. Any field not in the schema cannot be in the payload because nothing in the redactor reads from arbitrary maps. The telemetry adapter re-validates the payload against the schema before sending and rejects on extra keys (`.strict()`). A unit test fuzzes the redactor with payloads containing prompts, env values, and file paths and asserts none appear in the output.

This is what makes "no leaks" not a forecast: a leak requires modifying both the schema and the constructor in the same PR, which a CI test will catch.

### Apply executor: ordered, idempotent, rollback-first

1. Acquire `registries/.update.lock` (file lock; refuse concurrent applies).
2. Snapshot every path the plan will touch into `06-runs-and-logs/updates/<ts>/rollback/<original-relative-path>`, plus a `manifest.sha256.json` of pre-state.
3. For each PlanItem in plan order: re-evaluate policy (defense in depth), apply, write a per-item result record. On any failure, stop, run rollback, exit non-zero.
4. Write `agentic-os.lock.json` LAST. The lock update is the commit point — if power fails before, the next `update apply` sees the old lock and replays cleanly because every file write was preceded by a snapshot.
5. Release lock; run post-doctor; emit heartbeat with `last_apply` updated.

### Channels and defaults

| Channel | Default Policy (operator root) | Default Policy (customer root) | Telemetry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dev` | manual_only | (not allowed on customer) | local-only |
| `preview` | prompt_before_apply | manual_only | opt-in |
| `stable` | prompt_before_apply | safe_additive | opt-in (default ON for stable) |
| `pinned` | pinned_version | pinned_version | off |

Customer installs default to `stable`, NOT `pinned`. Rationale: most installs need security updates; `pinned` is for regulated cases that declare themselves. Operator can ship a `policy: pinned` declaration via `UPDATE_POLICY.md` per-install at provision time.

## Phases

### P1 — Local update apply with rollback (week 1–2, 2 weeks)

- Manifest types, lockfile reader/writer, plan builder.
- Policy evaluator (pure, fully unit-tested).
- Apply executor with snapshot+rollback.
- CLI: `update check`, `update plan`, `update apply`, `update rollback`, `update status`.
- Manifest source: git adapter only (read tag from source repo URL in lockfile).
- No telemetry yet. No signing yet (checksum-only).
- Doctor extensions: installed version, channel, last check/apply, rollback availability.

**Exit criteria:** an operator can `update apply` against a local OS root with a hand-crafted manifest, see the plan, see rollback artifacts, and undo with `update rollback --run <id>`.

### P2 — Phone home and fleet visibility (week 3–4, 2 weeks)

- Redactor + Heartbeat schema, schema-validated at both ends.
- HTTPS telemetry adapter; `update heartbeat` CLI; scheduled heartbeat job (cron-like, cadence per channel: dev=never, preview=daily, stable=hourly, pinned=never).
- Static HTTPS manifest adapter alongside git adapter; channel chooses adapter.
- Operator dashboard: read-only view over collected heartbeats (initially a CLI command `agentic-os fleet status` that hits the same collector).
- Rate limiting: heartbeat client backs off on 429/5xx with jitter; collector caps payload to 4KB and rejects above.

**Exit criteria:** ten test installs across two channels report into a collector; operator sees install_id, version, channel, capability_hash, doctor summary; no PII or prompts present in any captured payload (verified by collector-side schema strict check + a fuzzing test in CI).

### P3 — Customer fleet auto-apply with approval workflow (week 5–6, 2 weeks)

- Approval tokens: signed (ed25519) tokens generated by operator CLI, dropped into `registries/approvals/` on target install. Token names a migration id and an install_id (or `*` for fleet-wide).
- `UPDATE_POLICY.md` machine-parseable frontmatter (`permits:` list); doctor warns on stale permits.
- Manifest signing (manifest adapters verify ed25519 signature when present; warn-only in P3, enforce in v1.1).
- Per-customer policy bundling: customer install declares `customer_id`; operator dashboard groups by customer_id.
- Migration runner: migrations are named scripts in the package, executed only when their `requires_approval` is satisfied; each writes a marker into `06-runs-and-logs/updates/<ts>/migrations/<id>.json`.

**Exit criteria:** operator issues a single signed token, ten stable-channel customer installs auto-apply the migration on their next heartbeat-driven check, three of them roll back successfully via the rollback CLI, and the dashboard reflects all of it within 1 hour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `update apply` on a root without `.agentic_root` exits non-zero with code 2 and writes nothing. (Test: integration.)
2. `update apply` never overwrites `agentic-os.local.json` regardless of manifest contents. (Test: unit + integration.)
3. Every PlanItem applied by the executor has a corresponding `PolicyDecision == AUTO_APPLY` recorded in `06-runs-and-logs/updates/<ts>/decisions.json`. (Test: integration asserts 1:1.)
4. A PlanItem with `type: exec_change | hook_change | mcp_change | permission_change` on a customer install fails with `BLOCKED` unless an approval token or `UPDATE_POLICY.md` permit matches its migration id. (Test: unit on evaluator, integration on executor.)
5. Heartbeat payload sent to the telemetry adapter conforms to `HeartbeatPayload` schema (`.strict()`); extra keys cause the adapter to throw before sending. (Test: unit with fuzzed input.)
6. Heartbeat payload contains no value from `process.env`, no file contents from outside the install root, and no fields under `customer_id` unless `UPDATE_POLICY.md` opts in. (Test: property test that mutates env and FS, asserts payload unchanged.)
7. `update rollback --run <id>` restores every file recorded in that run's `manifest.sha256.json` to its pre-apply SHA. (Test: integration with byte-level diff.)
8. Concurrent `update apply` invocations against the same root: second exits non-zero with code 11 and changes nothing. (Test: integration with two processes.)
9. `agentic-os doctor` reports all nine fields listed in §Doctor. Missing any field is a doctor blocker, not a warning. (Test: snapshot.)
10. A manifest with `minimum_supported_version > installed_version` causes `update plan` to refuse with a clear error naming both versions. (Test: unit.)

## Validations

- **Unit:** policy.evaluator (all PlanItem types × all policies × approval present/absent), redactor (schema + fuzz), plan.builder (drift detection: file edited locally vs manifest expects original), rollback.snapshot (round-trip).
- **Integration (per phase):** P1 — full apply+rollback against a fixture root. P2 — heartbeat round-trip against an in-process collector with strict schema. P3 — multi-install fleet sim (10 installs in tmpdirs, one signed token, assert apply on all ten).
- **CI gate:** the redactor fuzz test runs on every PR. A new field added to the heartbeat schema requires a paired test asserting it is constructed from a named source, not copied from a map.
- **Manual:** before each release, operator runs `update apply` on their own dogfood root and confirms rollback works.

## Risks

1. **Drift between manifest schema and installed lockfile schema.** Mitigation: `schema_version` field on both; lockfile migration is itself a PlanItem with its own approval path.
2. **Apply mid-flight crash leaves install in mixed state.** Mitigation: lock-last commit; rollback snapshot precedes every write; `update status` detects in-progress runs (lock present, no completion record) and prompts to run `rollback`.
3. **Operator's signing key compromise.** Mitigation: tokens carry expiry; operator can publish a revocation list at a well-known URL; installs check the revocation list on every plan. (In v1, revocation list is opt-in; in v1.1 it is required.)
4. **Customer disables phone-home and falls behind on security updates without operator noticing.** Mitigation: `customer_id`-grouped dashboard surfaces "last heartbeat > 30d ago" as a yellow signal; no automatic action — operator decides.
5. **Telemetry endpoint leaks payloads on its own (logs, indexing).** Mitigation: collector is open-source and minimal; documented operational guidance to disable request body logging; payload is already redacted by source, so collector-side leak is limited to redacted fields.
6. **`UPDATE_POLICY.md` drifts from actual frontmatter parsing.** Mitigation: doctor parses it on every run and reports any unparseable line as a blocker.
7. **Apply executor races on heartbeat-driven check.** Mitigation: heartbeat job NEVER applies; it only checks and writes a notification record. Apply requires explicit CLI invocation OR a policy declaration that the install is in autonomous mode (separate flag, not in v1).

## What's NOT in v0

- Hosted update service. (P3 uses static HTTPS + git; hosted comes post-v1.)
- Notion-backed control plane. (Notion can mirror dashboard state, but is never a source of truth.)
- Auto-apply on customer roots without operator-issued approval token. (Listed as future flag; not in v1.)
- Cross-install migration coordination (e.g., "apply this only after install X reports ok"). (Out of scope; would require central state.)
- Binary diffing / delta updates. (Full-file replace with checksum verify.)
- Revocation list enforcement (opt-in in v1, mandatory v1.1).
- Signed manifest enforcement (warn-only in v1, mandatory v1.1).
- UI dashboard. (CLI `fleet status` in v1; web UI later.)
- Multi-tenant operator support (one operator identity per fleet in v1).

Focus: make the trust claims (no leaks, safe auto-apply, rollback works) backed by deterministic mechanisms (schema-constructed payloads, pure policy evaluator + executor refusal, snapshot-before-write with lock-last commit) rather than aspirational language.
